newsitem.title: USA: Barshefsky--China must improve WTO-related offer.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky--China must improve WTO-related offer.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative nominee Charlene Barshefsky said Wednesday the speed with which China joins the World Trade Organization will depend on whether that country improves offers currently on the table.

"The pace of China's accession negotiations depends very much on Beijing's willingness to improve the offers now on the table," Barshefsky said in prepared testimony for a Senate Finance Committee hearing on her nomination.
She added that it was in the interest of the United States for China to become a member of the WTO.

"The administration believes that it is in our interest that China become a member of the WTO; however, we have been steadfast in leading the effort to assure that China's accession to the WTO would occur on commercial, rather than political, grounds," she said.

Talks on Russia joining the WTO have been "quite positive and we look for more progress," Barshefsky said. "We are excited about the prospects of the accession of many of the former Soviet Republics and the Baltic States."
Saudi Arabia and Vietnam are also becoming more active, she said.
Barshefsky said there was "an urgent need to integrate Sub-Saharan Africa into the international trading system."
Achieving that goal lies in African countries reforming their economies and in the United States encouraging that process, she said.
"We are reviewing a range of options to promote this," she said.
Barshefsky's nomination to the post has been complicated by a law barring anyone from the post if they have represented a foreign government on trade matters.
She represented Canadian lumber interests while she was a Washington lawyer.
Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth said he supports a waiver of the law to allow Barshefsky to be confirmed.
She has been serving as acting U.S. Trade Representative since April last year.
